newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen down on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen down on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares on Thursday inched down after a four-session rise and analysts predicted at least one more session of profit-taking before the market, currently just above 15,000 points, rebounded.

"Tomorrow there could be another slight fall like today but I think the market should resume growth around Tuesday," said Wojciech Smolka, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage, who put support at around 14,500 points.
Analysts said this week's rises were likely linked with recent gains on Western bourses and that demand could rise next week before the release of firms' September earnings reports.

The main market's all-share WIG index inched down 0.2 points to 15,049.0 and turnover eased 1.5 percent to 140.9 million zlotys ($50.2 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 36 to 25 with 17 stocks flat.
Analysts said investors next week would also be watching September's year-on-year inflation figure due on Tuesday.
The central bank, which wants real interest rates to rise in the coming months, expects the September yearly figure to fall to around 19 percent from 20.5 percent after August.
Analysts said wood and furniture trader Paged could soon stabilise around the 18 zlotys ($6.4), or 50 percent above issue price, at which it started trade on Thursday.
They said biggest loser construction firm Elektromontaz Export, down 5.1 percent, may have been hurt by Wednesday's news of a planned new share issue earmarked for convertible bonds.
Continuous trade turnover was at about one million zlotys ($0.4 million) with biggest mover trader Universal down 3.6 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 4.4 percent to 167 zlotys ($59.4) in 54.2-million-zloty ($19.3 million) trade and were flat at 166 zlotys ($59.1) in 19.6-million-zloty ($7 million) live trade.
